explainer.heading: Sunscreen is built to stay put, including when it meets water
body: A sunscreen that works has to survive sweat and humidity all day — which is exactly what stops it rinsing away with water and a face wash.
What remains sits on the skin overnight, mixed with the day's oil and dust. This is one of the common causes of congestion across the forehead and chin in people who wear no make-up at all.
Micellar water works differently from a cleanser: micelles bind to oil and carry it off, so it lifts what water cannot. This bottle states pH 5.5 and is usable on eyes and lips.

blocks.heading: Three kinds of day, three different levels of need
blocks.intro: Not every day calls for this step equally. Said plainly so you do not overuse it.

items.heading: Make-up, or a lot of time in the sun
items.body: Not optional. Neither make-up nor sunscreen is water-soluble, and a cleanser alone will not lift all of it.

items.heading: Sunscreen only, indoors
items.body: Still worth it, but lighter — one cotton pad will do. Sunscreen is designed to stay put, including the kind worn indoors.

items.heading: Nothing applied, home all day
items.body: Not needed. Washing is enough. Adding a removal step on a day with nothing to remove only takes away natural oils.

blocks.heading: Two cleansing agents, six conditioning ones
blocks.intro: Make-up removal involves more friction against the skin than any other step of the day, so what accompanies the cleansing agent matters as much as the agent.

blocks.eyebrow: Where it sits in the day
blocks.heading: The first step of the evening, before the cleanser
blocks.intro: The order here is not flexible: remove first, cleanse second. Reverse it and the cleanser is carrying work it cannot do.

steps.label: No removal step needed
steps.note: Overnight your skin has only its own oil and sweat, which a cleanser handles.

steps.label: Wash with cool water
steps.note: Then carry on with your usual steps.

steps.label: Saturate the cotton pad evenly
steps.note: Evenly wet, not dripping. Dragging a dry pad across skin is friction you do not need.

steps.label: Hold it in place for a few seconds
steps.note: Especially on eyes and lips. Let the make-up soften before you wipe — wiping straight away is scrubbing.

steps.label: Wipe once, in one direction
steps.note: No back and forth. Use a fresh pad if colour still comes away.

steps.label: Follow with the cleanser
steps.note: This takes the remaining micelle residue and the excess oil.

blocks.footnote: If your eyes sting, it is usually from wiping before the make-up has softened rather than from the product. Hold the pad in place and count to five first.

blocks.heading: Two steps, evenings only
blocks.intro: The order and the cautions are taken from the manufacturer's instructions.

items.heading: Saturate a cotton pad
items.body: Wipe across the face, paying attention to the sides of the nose, the eye area and under the lip — the narrow places where residue is left behind.

items.heading: Then wash with the cleanser
items.body: Micellar water does not replace the wash step. Skip it and the remaining residue stays on the skin.

blocks.footnote: Patch-test on the neck and watch for 30–45 minutes before using it on the whole face. Do not rub hard: hand pressure does more harm than any ingredient in the bottle.

blocks.heading: Can micellar water replace a cleanser?
blocks.intro: No. The two steps lift different things, and each leaves work for the other.

items.q: Do I still need to wash afterwards?
items.a: Yes. The manufacturer's step two is to wash with a cleanser. Skip it and the residue stays on the skin.

items.q: Do I need this if I wear no make-up?
items.a: If you use sunscreen, yes. Sunscreen clings fairly firmly and a face wash alone often does not lift all of it.

items.q: Can I use it around the eyes?
items.a: The manufacturer positions it for the eye and lip area. Wipe gently, do not rub, and avoid getting it into the eye itself.
Somewhere dry and cool, away from direct sunlight and heat. Close the cap after use and keep out of reach of children.
